Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, hit store shelves on Friday to considerable lines and long wait times for pre-orders. But some customers who were lucky enough to get the $1,999-and-up phone on its first weekend have been reporting a pretty big problem: The inner screen of the phone can break, showing horizontal bright lines emanating from the phone's hinge. Apple on Monday said it was aware of the issue, which it said affected a "small number" of phones, and that it would replace the devices under its AppleCare warranty. "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units," an Apple representative told CNBC. "If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement." Apple says on its website that an inner-screen repair will be $999 for iPhone Duos that are out-of-warranty. Most of the reports are from anonymous customers on online forums such as Reddit and X , and there are fake images online as well. But well-respected device repair firm iFixit weighed in on Sunday, after tearing down the new device and testing its resistance to dust, and theorized the issues may have to do with Apple's hinge design. "Many of these damage reports describe folding or unfolding the phone, hearing a crunch, and pushing past it," said iFixit technician Shahram Mokhtari in its teardown video . "Right where the damage is happening, the hinge is shaped a little differently." "The hinge is actually dozens of parts, with ludicrous precision," iFixit CEO Kyle Wiens posted on X. "A manufacturing variance or grain of sand can kill the fragile display panel it protects." watch now VIDEO 1:41 01:41 Display issues on iPhone duo TechCheck Breaking screens have been an issue with foldable phones going back to 2019, and have been seen as one of the major roadblocks to the technology's widespread adoption. That year, Samsung released one of its first folding devices, and reviewers quickly found that its inner screen cracked during normal use. Early reviewers praised the experience of using the iPhone Duo when unfolded, especially for multitasking or media, but said that many apps had not been updated to take full advantage of the phone's larger and wider screens. Apple said on Monday that apps were already being updated for the new foldable device. headlines.summary: Microsoft is trying to balance a rapid AI infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency.
headlines.article_text: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts as AI leads to efficiency push Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Around 60,000 Microsoft employees are eligible for the new buyout program across four countries, said a person familiar with the matter. The move comes six months after Microsoft announced its first-ever voluntary retirement program to a small set of U.S. workers. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:40 01:40 Microsoft offering buyouts to some employees in U.S., Canada, India and U.K. Squawk on the Street Microsoft said Monday that it's offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. The software maker announced a new voluntary exit offer for certain workers in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom at its experience level of 70 or below. Around 60,000 people are eligible, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be named while discussing an internal matter. The effort affects about 27% of Microsoft's total workforce of 223,000 people. Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies. That put a strain on Microsoft's finances. In April, it announced a first-ever voluntary retirement program that around 7% of U.S. employees were eligible for. Then, in July, Microsoft announced plans to lay off 4,800 employees . "The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees . "This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program." Microsoft is in the midst of a business model transformation , increasingly trying to charge clients based on how much AI they actually use. It has armed programmers, sellers and supply chain workers with AI tools and observed noticeable results . At the same time, the 51-year-old maker of Windows and Office wants to ensure that it has the right talent to go after its most compelling new growth opportunities. The idea is to make the shift without weakening Microsoft's financial profile. In the second quarter, cloud rivals Alphabet and Amazon both reported negative free cash flow, but Microsoft showed $19.64 billion in positive free cash flow for the period, down 23% year over year. Some marketing, sales and engineering teams have decided not to participate in the new buyout, the person said. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31, the person added. More than 30% of those who could join the voluntary retirement program went ahead with it, Microsoft said in July . But that was open to those at the senior director level and below, while the new initiative goes higher, to the vice president level, said the person briefed on the new plan. The person said Microsoft does not have a target in mind this time around. On Wednesday, Microsoft is scheduled to report third-quarter results. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Lockheed, JetBlue, CoreWeave, Surgery Partners & more Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out some of the companies making the biggest moves midday: Lockheed Martin — The prime defense contractor gained 3%. The future is bright following a deal to continue producing F-35 fighter jets for the Defense Department, Morgan Stanley said in an upgrade to overweight from equal weight while raising its 12-month price target to $835 from $690, suggesting 38% upside from Friday's close. CACI International — The defense contractor surged 6% after Jefferies upgraded CACI to buy from hold and raised its price target to $725, implying nearly 17% upside from Friday's close. JetBlue Airways —The New York-based airline tumbled 12% following a Wall Street Journal report that senior creditors for JetBlue are working with a restructuring advisor. The company's bond prices sank late last week, while its stock is down roughly 50% year to date. Verizon Communications — The telecommunications company fell 3% after reporting third-quarter earnings. Xencor — Shares surged 20% to a 52-week high of $30 after the biotech presented positive data on a therapy for certain types of kidney cancer. Xencor said its XmAb819 showed anti-tumor activity in patients with advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma, and said existing cash reserves are sufficient to fund pipeline research and operations into 2029. Neocloud stocks — Shares of several companies gained after Elon Musk said in a post on X that "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death." CoreWeave and Iren rebounded 5%, while Nebius added 1%. Tesla — The electric vehicle maker climbed 6% after Barclays upgraded Tesla to overweight. Analysts at the bank said a merger opportunity with SpaceX, growth in the Robotaxi business and core business strength made them more bullish on the outlook. Range Resources — The natural gas company rose 15% after EQT Corp announced it would buy the company in a deal that values Range Resources at more than $50 billion. Shares of EQT fell 4%. The all-stock deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Moderna — Shares fell another 2% after a sell-off following the leak of results from a closely followed cancer vaccine study last Thursday continued. The stock tumbled more than 18% over Thursday and Friday last week. Booz Allen Hamilton — The management and defense consultant rallied 8% after an upgrade to buy from hold with a $95 price target at TD Cowen, which cited improved "funded backlog, fed civilian sales and fixed price trends." Ross Stores — The retailer added 3% after UBS upgraded Ross to buy. Analysts at the bank said growing store productivity will help send the stock above $300. Surgery Partners — Shares surged 47% after Bon Secours Mercy Health agreed to a buyout at $23.50 a share in cash, or $5.7 billion. Fair Isaac — The data analytics company sank 14% after Wells Fargo downgraded Fair Isaac to equal weight from overweight. Analysts justified the downgrade after Fair Isaac said it wouldn't raise prices to encourage lenders to keep using its FICO score. Maplebear – The parent company of delivery service Instacart fell almost 6%.
